outlook.statement: The successful implementation of the restructuring scheme has strengthened the Company's revival process and improved its financial position. The management remains focused on completing the remaining settlement formalities with lenders and pursuing business opportunities aligned with the evolving economic conditions. As a result, the Company's operational capabilities.
The Company continues to evaluate opportunities in the infrastructure and construction sector while emphasizing prudent financial management, project execution and sustainable growth.
The Board remains focused on recovery of receivables, resolution of project and lender-related matters, preservation of asset value and revival of sustainable business operations.
The implementation of the Scheme and the completion of the remaining obligations are material to the Company's financial position and ability to continue operations.
The management's assessment is based on the expected successful implementation of the Scheme, recovery of outstanding receivables, resolution of project exposures and future business prospects.

The business outlook and initiatives proposed by the Management to address its financial risks have been discussed in detail in the Management Discussion and Analysis Report which forms the part of the Annual Report and annexed elsewhere in the Report.
remains committed to completing the resolution process, strengthening governance and controls, recovering outstanding amounts and pursuing sustainable business operations.

The Executive Directors have voluntarily waived their entitlement to remuneration for the financial years ended March 31, 2026, and March 31, 2025, reflecting their commitment to the long-term interests of the Company and its stakeholders.

The management believes that SPITPL has substantial contractual claims against NHAI arising from the concession agreement and assessment of the project, the outcome of which is expected to result in significant recoveries. Considering the merits of the claims, internal legal opinions obtained, progress of the arbitration proceedings, expected future cash flows from such recoveries and ongoing resolution process of SPITPL, the management is of the view that the underlying value of SPITPL is significantly higher than its presently reported net worth and that its net worth does not represent its fair or realizable value.

The aggregate value of performance obligations that are completely or partially unsatisfied as at 31 March 2026 is ₹ 1,29,266.00 lakhs, of which approximately 40% is expected to be recognized as revenue within the next one year and the remaining thereafter.

Management is of the view that going concern basis of accounting is appropriate based on partial implementation of Scheme of Arrangement, future business continuity and growth prospects, exit of majority of financial creditors and other mitigating factors.
The Holding Company is in discussions with the remaining three lenders and has filed an application before the Court seeking an extension of time for final settlement with these lenders.

Based on the expectation of successful implementation of the aforesaid scheme and the Group's future business growth prospects, the Management has prepared the consolidated financial results on a going concern basis.

risks: Intense competitive landscape resulting in pressure on project margins and bidding competitiveness
Project execution and approval risks: Delays in land acquisition, regulatory clearances, environmental approvals, utility shifting and contractual dependencies may impact project timelines and costs

Volatility in input costs: Fluctuations in the prices of key construction materials such as steel, cement, fuel and bitumen, together with labour cost inflation, could adversely affect project profitability

Funding and liquidity constraints: Infrastructure projects generally require substantial working capital and long gestation periods. Challenges in obtaining timely financing or fluctuations in interest rates may impact operational flexibility

Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainties: Changes in economic conditions, inflationary pressures, global supply chain disruptions and geopolitical developments may influence investment activity and project execution schedules
Regulatory and policy risks: Amendments to laws, taxation policies, environmental regulations and compliance requirements may affect project economics and business operations
Counterparty and recovery risks: Delays in receipt of project payments, claims realization and settlement of contractual disputes may impact cash flows and working capital management

Going concern and revival-related risks: While considerable progress has been achieved under the approved debt restructuring framework, successful completion of the remaining lender settlements and sustained operational revival remain critical to the Company's long-term growth strategy

The absence of final No Dues Certificates from the remaining lenders as at the reporting date may give rise to material uncertainty that could cast significant doubt on the Company's ability to continue as a going concern if the outstanding obligations are not fully discharged within the extended timeline.
The Company's operational results continued to be affected by the financial stress and legacy project exposures.
Trade receivables include long-outstanding amounts, including amounts relating to completed or substantially completed projects, subject to confirmations and adjustments.

The Company's exposure to Supreme Infrastructure BOT Private Limited and Supreme Panvel Indapur Tollways Private Limited, including investments, receivables and other balances, is dependent on the underlying project assets, contractual claims, arbitration proceedings, resolution processes and recoveries at the relevant special purpose vehicle level.

Outstanding corporate guarantees aggregating to Rs 1,51,347.85 lakhs as at 31 March 2026. Any subsequent developments, invocation, settlement or release of such guarantees shall be evaluated and disclosed.

Revenue from operations during the year was Rs 6,533.86 lakhs as compared with Rs 6,616.56 lakhs in the previous year.

The Scheme of Compromise and Arrangement under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013, between the Company and its financial creditors was sanctioned by the Company Court, by order dated 28 March 2025.
Payments have been completed in respect of 11 out of 14 financial creditors, and the relevant lenders have issued final No Dues Certificates and completed applicable charge-release formalities.
Substantial payments have been made to the remaining three lenders, in respect of which final No Dues Certificates and/or completion of related formalities remained pending as at 31 March 2026.

Exceptional items for the year include accounting gains arising from the reversal of interest and principal in connection with partial implementation of the Scheme, reversal of interest relating to lenders whose final No Dues Certificates remained pending, and other settlement-related items.
The Company reported positive total equity of Rs 23,723.24 lakhs as at 31 March 2026; however, it has significant accumulated losses and continuing operational and financial challenges.

During the year, pursuant to shareholders' approval dated 21 October 2024, the Company issued 7,10,37,388 equity shares of Rs 10 each at an issue price of Rs 86.94 per share, including a premium of Rs 76.94 per share, through preferential allotment.

The Company also allotted 2,21,12,953 warrants convertible into an equivalent number of equity shares at an issue price of Rs 86.94 per warrant. During the quarter ended 31 March 2026, 7,67,000 warrants were converted into equity shares.
The Board does not recommend any dividend for the financial year ended 31 March 2026.
The Company is not proposing to transfer any amount to the General Reserves of the Company out of the profits made during the year.
Ten meetings of the Board of Directors were held during the year under review. The intervening gap between two consecutive Board Meetings did not exceed 120 days.
